characters.description: The Sun Summoner, a Grisha able to call light and the one prophesied to destroy the Shadow Fold. Once an overlooked orphan and army mapmaker, she now carries a powerful amplifier taken from Morozova's stag and the weight of what her gift means to Ravka. Having escaped the Darkling's attempt to enslave her power, she begins this book in exile across the sea with Mal, hunted, unsure how to use her light against an enemy who is far older and more cunning than she is.
characters.name: Alina Starkov

characters.description: Alina's oldest friend and the finest tracker in Ravka's army, who fled with her after the events at the Little Palace. Devoted to Alina, he has given up his old life to keep her safe, but the gulf between an ordinary soldier and the living saint she is becoming has begun to strain them. His tracking skill remains vital as the hunt for further sources of power continues.
characters.name: Malyen Oretsev

characters.description: The ageless leader of the Grisha, who commands shadow and who created the Shadow Fold long ago with forbidden magic. In the previous book he sought to bind Alina's light to his will and turn the Fold into a weapon of conquest, and she barely escaped him. Ruthless, patient, and immensely powerful, he remains the greatest threat to Alina and to Ravka, and he has not given up his design for her or for the country.
characters.name: The Darkling

characters.description: The unsettling priest who served at the Ravkan court as the king's spiritual adviser and took a keen interest in the religious meaning others attached to the Sun Summoner. Watchful and hard to read, he moves according to his own beliefs and loyalties, and the fervent devotion ordinary people feel toward Alina as a saint plays into his aims.
characters.name: The Apparat

characters.description: A beautiful young Grisha with the rare gift of a Tailor, able to reshape appearance and flesh, who befriended Alina at the Little Palace. In the previous book she was revealed to have acted as the Darkling's agent within the royal household, a betrayal that complicates any trust between her and Alina going forward.
characters.name: Genya

characters.description: A proud and beautiful Grisha Squaller who commands wind and was among the elite trained at the Little Palace. Sharp-tongued and once openly contemptuous of Alina, she is a skilled and formidable fighter whose loyalties, in the wreckage the Darkling has left, are no longer simple.
characters.name: Zoya

characters.description: A famous and daring privateer captain, clever, quick-tongued, and unpredictable, who sails the northern seas with a loyal and unusually capable crew. He crosses paths with Alina and Mal in the midst of danger and proves willing to defy even the most feared powers when it suits his own designs. His true purposes are not what they first appear, and he has ambitions far larger than piracy.
characters.name: Sturmhond

characters.description: A giant of a young man in Sturmhond's crew, one of a pair of twins, and a Grisha as well as a warrior. Physically imposing and surprisingly thoughtful, fond of poetry, he serves the privateer captain with fierce loyalty and becomes one of the fighters drawn into Alina's cause.
characters.name: Tolya Yul-Bataar

characters.description: Tolya's twin sister, a fierce and skilled warrior in Sturmhond's crew who fights with paired axes, and a Grisha like her brother. Sharp and watchful, she is devoted to the captain and, with Tolya, becomes part of the small band that gathers around the Sun Summoner.
characters.name: Tamar Kir-Bataar

recaps.ending: The Darkling, alive and more dangerous than before, now commands a host of shadow creatures born of forbidden magic. After he forces Alina onto a sea hunt for a second amplifier, the privateer captain Sturmhond helps her and Mal escape, and Alina claims the power of the sea whip, adding a second amplifier to the stag's antlers. Sturmhond is revealed to be Prince Nikolai Lantsov, a younger son of Ravka's royal house working to save the country from collapse, and he returns Alina to the capital. There she becomes the reluctant symbol and leader of the Second Army and an object of religious devotion the Apparat cultivates, while Nikolai maneuvers to secure the crown, proposing an alliance and marriage with her for the good of the realm. The bond between Alina and Mal frays as power and duty pull her away from him. The book ends in catastrophe: the Darkling assaults the capital with his shadow soldiers and takes the city. Nikolai is grievously attacked and disappears, Alina's power falters at the worst moment, and she is led underground by the Apparat's devoted followers, weakened and cornered. The hope of stopping the Darkling now rests on finding a third amplifier, the firebird, and the balance has tipped sharply in the enemy's favor.
recaps.in_short: Hiding across the sea with Mal, Alina is captured by the Darkling, who has survived and now commands terrible shadow soldiers. He forces her onto a hunt for a legendary sea creature whose body holds a second amplifier. The privateer captain Sturmhond turns on the Darkling and helps Alina and Mal escape, and Alina claims the sea whip's power as her second amplifier, growing stronger. Sturmhond is revealed to be Prince Nikolai Lantsov of Ravka, and he brings them back to the capital. There Alina is made the figurehead of the Second Army and a saint to the common people, whose devotion the priest known as the Apparat encourages, while Nikolai schemes to save the failing kingdom and proposes binding himself to Alina to secure the throne. Mal grows ever more distant as Alina is consumed by power and politics. The Darkling attacks the capital with his shadow monsters and overwhelms it. Nikolai is gravely assailed and vanishes, and Alina, her strength faltering, is taken underground by the Apparat's followers, with the search now turned toward a third and final amplifier, the firebird.

recaps.text: Previously, in Shadow and Bone: Alina Starkov, an overlooked orphan serving as an army mapmaker, discovered she was the Sun Summoner, a Grisha able to conjure light and, by legend, the only one who could destroy the Shadow Fold that splits Ravka. Taken by the Darkling, the ageless leader of the Grisha, she was trained at the Little Palace and drawn to his power and attention. But she learned the truth: the Darkling had created the Fold himself with forbidden magic and meant to use her light to turn it into a weapon of conquest. Alina fled and, with the help of her oldest friend and tracker Mal, sought Morozova's stag, a legendary creature whose antlers could be forged into an amplifier to increase her power. The Darkling caught them, killed the stag, and fastened its antler collar on Alina to control her, then used her light to kill on the Fold. Discovering the bond ran both ways, Alina seized command of her own power, broke his hold, and escaped with Mal across the Fold and out of Ravka. The Darkling was left behind but not destroyed, and Alina now carried the stag's amplifier and the burden of what she was.

Alina and Mal have been living in hiding far from Ravka, across the sea, trying to disappear into ordinary life. Their refuge does not last: the Darkling, who survived their last encounter and now commands frightening new shadow creatures, tracks them down and takes them captive. He forces Alina onto a dangerous sea hunt in search of a second amplifier, a legendary creature whose power could be joined to the amplifier she already carries and make her light greater still, though bound once more to his will. Aboard ship and closely guarded, Alina and Mal look for any chance to break free, and help arrives from an unexpected quarter in the form of a bold and cunning privateer captain and his crew, whose willingness to cross even the Darkling opens a narrow path to escape.

characters.description: An Earth-born Unbound altered into a Nemean. Banished into the void after surviving the essence-anchor crisis, he receives a quest to escape and carries Ravenous Tithe, an ability that consumes claimed targets and their power.
characters.name: Felix Nevarre

characters.description: Felix's bonded Tenku companion, stranded beside him in the void. Pit fights at Felix's side as they search for a way to escape.
characters.name: Pit

characters.description: A weakened primordial bound to Felix through power he consumed. The Maw cannot strike him physically in the void, but remains a hostile and knowledgeable adviser who seeks influence over him.
characters.name: The Maw

characters.description: A powerful corrupted void creature carrying much of the Maw's stolen power. The Maw's reaction draws it toward Felix Nevarre and Pit, and it begins pursuing them.
characters.name: The Corrupted Gnarhollow

characters.description: A dwarf pirate officer who commands a schooner's attack after its crew notices Felix and Pit in the void.
characters.name: The dwarf pirate officer

characters.description: A dwarf officer who commands a pirate schooner's attack on Felix and Pit. He belongs to the Ten Hands and captains the Night's Wake.
characters.name: The Night's Wake captain

characters.description: The heir of Pax Rell, a guild trainee, and a survivor of Magda's Foglands expedition. At the tribunal, she credits Magda's group with rescuing abandoned prisoners and challenges the guild's refusal to help them.
characters.name: Vessilia Dayne

characters.description: The missing leader of the Foglands rescue expedition. Her actions saved prisoners abandoned by the guild, while her surviving associates face judgment in her absence.
characters.name: Magda Aren

characters.description: A member of the group caught in the tribunal's aftermath. She remains with the Foglands survivors while Magda Aren and Felix Nevarre are missing.
characters.name: Evie Aren

characters.description: Magda's former teammate and one of the Foglands survivors facing the guild tribunal. He belongs to the group left to manage the consequences while Magda and Felix remain missing.
characters.name: Harn Kastos

characters.description: The Harwatch guild's Elder of Acquisitions. During the tribunal, she defends the guild's decision not to mount a rescue after its Foglands operation lost contact.
characters.name: Eliza DuFont

characters.description: Vessilia Dayne’s guardian, who removes her from the guild tribunal after she challenges the council.
characters.name: Vessilia Dayne’s guardian

characters.description: The Nixie ruler of the Ten Hands stronghold and Felix's captor. He offers Felix a place among the pirates after the Night's Wake brings the unusual newcomer before him.
characters.name: The Ten Hands captain

characters.description: A naiad cook in the Ten Hands stronghold. She recognizes Pit as a Tenku and gives him mana-rich food, showing him respect uncommon among Felix's captors.
characters.name: Dahlia

characters.description: An ogre enforcer serving the Ten Hands captain. He is identified as a dangerous journeyman-level member of the pirate leadership.
characters.name: Korm Rocksplitter

characters.description: A disturbed human and former Sage of Vellus living in the void. His fragmented knowledge points Felix toward a temple near desolation as a possible route of escape.
characters.name: Daedalus Mungle

characters.description: A fire mage and Foglands survivor studying under a Harwatch elder. His association with the expedition draws the attention of hostile noble apprentices.
characters.name: Atar V'as

characters.description: The leader of the Harwatch guild branch. He views the changed Foglands as an opening for territorial growth and access to newly available resources.
characters.name: High Elder Fairbanks

characters.description: A Harwatch guild elder directing research into inert primordial essence found in Foglands survivors. The elder proposes extracting and studying it through a concealed program.
characters.name: Elder of Spirit

characters.description: A Sworn agent employed by Eliza DuFont. The assignment combines Vessilia Dayne's protection with the intended killing of Magda Aren.
characters.name: The Sworn operative

characters.description: A Ten Hands scout who secretly follows Felix with a silent elf companion under concealment wards. The pair report on Felix's strength and handling of his damaged ship.
characters.name: The half-orc pirate bard

characters.description: A silent elf who trails Felix Nevarre alongside a half-orc scout. Concealment wards hide the pair while they observe Felix for the Ten Hands captain.
characters.name: The silent elf observer

characters.description: A corva rim worker who brings Felix and Pit to Echo's Reach. Impressed by Felix's restraint and his voluntary pact with Pit, he offers to house both newcomers.
characters.name: The corva ferryman

characters.description: The ferryman who shelters Felix and Pit at his three-island farm in Echo's Reach. He maintains the household with his spouse and children.
characters.name: The corva farmer

characters.description: A corva farmkeeper and parent who shares a three-island farm with the ferryman. She welcomes Felix and Pit into the family household.
characters.name: The corva farmkeeper

characters.description: Vessilia Dayne's former betrothed and current combat instructor, acting for her father. The Hand confines her interests to her family's plans and presses her to abandon her Foglands allies.
characters.name: The duke's Hand

characters.description: A guild archivist who lets Vessilia Dayne overhear news of the hidden Foglands survivors by manipulating a privacy ward, then restores the ward while watching how she responds.
characters.name: The guild archivist

characters.description: An Echo's Reach leader who intervenes when conference guards provoke Felix, disciplines them, and receives Felix and Pit privately.
characters.name: The conference lord

characters.description: The Master Inquisitor commanding the Inquisition contingent that arrives in Harwatch. He announces an operation against Foglands monsters and demonstrates authority backed by overwhelming mana.
characters.name: Corrin Catan

characters.description: Vessilia Dayne’s guardian. He restricts her contact with guild members he has not approved.
characters.name: Darius

characters.description: A concealed survivor who watches Magda's body being removed from the guild ward. Hidden by illusion and aided by inherited arrays, he evades the group while pursuing a plan associated with his father.
characters.name: The unidentified envoy

characters.description: A living dwarf imprisoned within a pirate ship's mana engine and drained as its power source. The vessel cannot be operated normally while the captive remains connected.
characters.name: The imprisoned dwarf

characters.description: An Echo's Reach conference leader rescued by Felix from a pirate mana engine. He survives the extraction but is left nearly unresponsive by his captivity.
characters.name: Lord Knowledge

recaps.ending: Felix and Pit return to the continent through the ruined temple's blood gate. The Maw crosses with them and confronts an unidentified chained presence, leaving its fate and Felix's primordial connection unresolved. Felix's dependence on Ravenous Tithe and his advancing bloodline processing also remain dangerous. The Ten Hands captain is dead, many captives are free, and Dahlia escapes alone, but Korm's fate and the whereabouts of the corva farmer's spouse and children are unknown. In Harwatch, Evie, Harn, and their companions cremate Magda. The Inquisition seals the Hargate and controls Foglands access, while the guild's concealed primordial-essence experiments continue in a desert domain. The imprisoned unidentified envoy deliberately infects another prisoner with blood-red primordial rot, advancing an unexplained plan connected to his father.
recaps.in_short: Banished into the void with Pit and the weakened Maw, Felix Nevarre learns to control his mana, escapes the Ten Hands pirates, and finds temporary refuge in Echo's Reach. In Harwatch, Magda Aren's allies uncover the guild's secret exploitation of Foglands survivors and recover Magda's preserved body. Echo's Reach leaders blame and banish Felix, after which he learns that the Ten Hands engineered the attacks. The pirates destroy the settlement and enslave its people as mana sources. Felix pursues the raiders, frees many captives, destroys their ships, and kills their corrupted captain. He and Pit then reach a ruined temple and activate a blood gate with the pursuing whale maw's blood, returning to the continent. Magda is cremated, but the guild's experiments continue despite the Inquisition's arrival. An unidentified imprisoned envoy begins spreading primordial rot, while the Maw confronts a vast chained presence after the crossing.

recaps.text: Previously: Felix Nevarre, an Earth-born Unbound changed into a Nemean, fought beside his bonded Tenku companion, Pit, in the Foglands. Magda Aren led an expedition that rescued prisoners abandoned by the guild, but the operation left Felix, Magda, and others missing.

Felix and Pit awaken in the void with the weakened Maw, which is bound to Felix and unable to harm him directly. An escape quest gives them their only clear objective. Harrowings drain their power, while Ravenous Tithe lets Felix consume claimed creatures and release stolen mana. A corrupted Gnarhollow carrying much of the Maw's lost strength hunts them across floating stone islands. Felix diverts it and begins learning to regulate his leaking mana through internal gates. Mortal contact brings a different threat. Pirates aboard the Night's Wake attack, capture Felix and Pit, and carry them to the Ten Hands stronghold, where the Nixie captain recruits Felix under coercive conditions. On the continent, Vessilia Dayne testifies before the guild tribunal. She admits Magda concealed the rescue expedition's purpose but condemns the guild for abandoning its people and credits Magda and Harn Kastos with saving prisoners. The hearing leaves Magda's surviving allies facing punishment while Magda and Felix remain missing.

Inside the Ten Hands stronghold, Felix conceals his abilities while the captain probes his Nemean identity. Pit discovers that living captives are drained to power pirate ships, and Felix realizes the captain may intend the same use for him. Dahlia, a naiad cook who reveres Pit as a Tenku, provides food and later helps the pair evade pursuit. Daedalus Mungle points Felix toward a temple near desolation as a possible exit. Felix and Pit steal a small manaship, but the pirate flagship pursues them and badly damages it before they escape deeper into the void. In Harwatch, the tribunal expels Magda's surviving associates from the guild. Evie Aren grieves her sister's reported death, while Harn and the displaced group plan to rebuild and eventually leave the city. Atar V'as, another Foglands survivor, continues his apprenticeship under a guild elder and draws the interest of hostile noble apprentices.

Harwatch's High Elder Fairbanks treats the cleared Foglands as an opportunity for expansion. With the Elder of Spirit, he authorizes secret experiments on inert primordial essence found in ill survivors. The discussion also confirms Eliza DuFont's involvement with the operative sent to ensure Magda's death while protecting Vessilia. Atar later enters a restricted ward, hears a survivor begging for death, and finds Magda's unresponsive body preserved by arrays. He is threatened into silence. Meanwhile, Felix's failing ship reaches a domain boundary and survives another creature attack. A corva ferryman then brings Felix and Pit to Echo's Reach. The settlement grants conditional sanctuary after Pit demonstrates that his pact with Felix is voluntary, and the ferryman houses them on his farm. Felix works on his mana gates and damaged mental defenses, but learns that Ravenous Tithe feeds on his own body, mind, and spirit when deprived. Echo's Reach offers shelter and a repaired vessel, though its void-born residents have deteriorating core spaces and no proven route home.

Vessilia, confined under her guardian's authority, learns that the guild is concealing the Foglands survivors and resolves to investigate. At Echo's Reach, Felix helps defend farms and Rim Hunters from a sudden wave of void-beast attacks. Each use of Ravenous Tithe increases his bloodline processing, while prolonged exposure to the void weakens his regeneration. Conference records provide maps and evidence that desolations can eject material from other realms, but no reliable escape route. When the outer wardstones drain far too early, Felix accompanies the corva farmer to inspect them. A Noctnatter destroys their skimmer and injures the farmer before Felix kills and consumes it. Echo's Reach leaders then accuse Felix of sabotaging the wards and directing the attacks. Despite the farmer's defense, they seize Felix's ship and possessions, banish him beyond the wards, and separate him from Pit.

Atar's warning brings Evie and Vessilia together to investigate the guild's tenth floor. The arrival of Master Inquisitor Corrin Catan disrupts Harwatch and gives them an opening. They discover that guild personnel have moved the surviving subjects and are destroying evidence. Atar breaks the arrays protecting Magda's preserved body, allowing the group to remove her, while an unidentified envoy watches from concealment and continues a plan associated with his father. Beyond Echo's Reach, Felix learns from the Noctnatter's memory that the Ten Hands deliberately drove monsters through the wardstone. He captures a ship commanded by the half-orc pirate bard and discovers that its mana engine is bound to an imprisoned dwarf. Pit then warns him of the raid. Back at Echo's Reach, Felix finds fires, ruined homes, and a population carried away by the pirates. The corva farmer dies after confirming that his spouse and children were seized. Felix buries his host and commits to pursuing the abductors.

Felix attacks the fleeing pirate ships and releases many of Echo's Reach's captives, including Lord Knowledge, though the conference leader is nearly unresponsive. The farmer's spouse and children are not among those found. With Pit protecting the rescued prisoners, Felix draws void beasts toward the remaining fleet and boards the captain's flagship. Dahlia refuses to defend the pirates. Felix blinds Korm Rocksplitter and knocks him overboard, kills the captain's assassin, binds the captain, and drains the ship's mana engine. The corrupted whale maw destroys the flagship and nearby vessels, but Dahlia rescues Felix and Pit before departing alone on a skimmer. The captain returns aboard Felix's cutter, transformed by primordial essence, and Felix kills him. Still pursued by the whale maw and corrupted creatures, Felix and Pit head for the suspected temple near desolation as their last apparent route out of the void.

Felix and Pit enter the desolation's sheath, survive an immense serpent guardian, and crash on the island containing the broken temple. Inside, they find an inverted ruin associated with Vellus and a dormant blood gate to the corporeal realm. As corrupted creatures overwhelm the temple, Felix wounds the whale maw through the wall and uses its blood and power to activate the gate. He and Pit cross safely and return to the continent. The Maw crosses as well, then confronts a vast chained presence, leaving its status unresolved. In Harwatch, the Inquisition seals the Hargate and restricts Foglands travel to holders of its writs. Harn, Evie, and their companions cremate Magda. Evie and one companion mourn her as family. The guild's experiments on restrained subjects are moved to a controlled desert domain rather than ended. The unidentified envoy, now imprisoned, contaminates another prisoner's food with stored blood-red primordial rot and begins spreading the infection in service of his still-unknown plan.

characters.description: The book's viewpoint character, a reserved and calculating young man from the Argento auction family, enrolling at Quest Academy. His silver eyes let him appraise any object in exact detail and, far more rarely, observe and replicate other people's essence abilities. Guarded after a history of friendships that soured once people learned what he could do, he arrives ambivalent about becoming a hero at all.
characters.name: Salvatore "Sal" Argento

characters.description: A first-year cadet whose eyes turn fully white when she uses her foresight, a draining power that shows glimpses of specific people's possible futures. Ranked near the very top of the intake, she is candid, quick-witted and a little self-deprecating, and becomes Sal's closest confidant after the two agree to set their ranks aside and be genuine friends.
characters.name: Divinity Khan

characters.description: Sal's parents and the co-owners of Argento Auction, a respected appraisal and artifact business. Petro is warm, joking and business-minded, with an appraisal ability of his own; Sophia is more anxious and protective, and carries a restoration power that can mend damaged items. Both want Sal to choose his own path rather than inherit theirs.
characters.name: Petro and Sophia Argento

characters.description: A blonde cadet living on Sal's dorm floor, rattled by a low preliminary rank and anxious about how her parents will take it. Prickly at first but quick to warm, she briefly mistakes the immaculately turned-out Sal for a staff member.
characters.name: Hannah

characters.description: A considerate, sandy-haired cadet on Sal's floor who holds the dorm elevator for stragglers at the cost of his own standing. Low-ranked and easygoing, he is one of Sal's first acquaintances at the Academy.
characters.name: Kane

characters.description: A friendly, powerful guardian at the induction, reputed to be the world's foremost telepath. He tests the sincerity of Sal's apology after a chance collision, then introduces himself warmly and takes an early, encouraging interest in him. He is rumored to have a daughter even more powerful than himself.
characters.name: Nero

characters.description: The workshop's resident crafting lecturer, known by her hero alias. Her ability turns her gear and body into a suit of powered mechanical armor, drawn from a pendant core. Playful and flirtatious but exacting about quality, she becomes Sal's crafting mentor once she recognizes how extraordinary his ability is.
characters.name: Upgrade

characters.description: The headmaster of Quest Academy, who goes by a chosen name. His power reads and quantifies people's essence signatures, the basis for the standardized grading the guilds now rely on. He runs the semester as a strict, merit-only contest and takes a personal interest in the Academy's most unusual students.
characters.name: Quest

characters.description: The vice-captain of the Reavers Guild, a striking woman with dark red hair who carries a top-grade blade. She uses a fear-based ability as an informal character test on Sal, then, impressed by his composure and his appraisal skill, grants him a Reavers token marking him as a preferred supplier.
characters.name: Villa

characters.description: A broker on the Academy's internal trading floor. Sharp and persuasive, cautious at first about backing an unproven first-year, she becomes an eager and protective advocate once she grasps the value of Sal's crafting, and helps him manage his work under his "Myth" alias.
characters.name: Vanessa

characters.description: A confident cadet and aspiring controller-class team captain, first seen briefly enthralling Sal with what appears to be a charm ability before releasing him with an apology. Socially dominant and used to being the center of attention, she takes a persistent, teasing interest in Sal.
characters.name: Victoria Chase

characters.description: The instructor of the Academy's mandatory survival module, a hero whose ability is demon shapeshifting. He opens his first class by transforming into a fast, pack-hunting demon and violently subduing four overconfident volunteers - a brutal lesson that the sheltered cohort is nowhere near ready for the dangers beyond the barriers.
characters.name: Sinclair

characters.description: A resentful fellow cadet who confronts Sal in a restroom during the enrollment mixer after being laughed at, and throws the first punch. Sal exploits his poor stance and knocks him out with a single strike, making an enemy on his very first day at the Academy.
characters.name: The Day-One Rival

characters.description: A very low-ranked cadet given the grim nickname "The Necromancer." Withdrawn and frightened, she hears voices others cannot and fears she is losing her mind. Sal and Divinity single her out as a student worth saving and set out to earn her trust.
characters.name: Melanie Delahunt

characters.description: A low-ranked cadet picked onto Sal's five-person tournament squad in the combat-class draft. Sharp-tongued and funny, quick with a needling joke at his captain's expense.
characters.name: Barry Francis

characters.description: A low-ranked cadet picked onto Sal's five-person tournament squad in the combat-class draft. Steady, dependable and self-effacing.
characters.name: Jack Brophy

characters.description: A low-ranked cadet picked onto Sal's five-person tournament squad in the combat-class draft. Easily flustered, and earnest about proving she belongs.
characters.name: Blathnaid McClean

characters.description: A low-ranked cadet picked onto Sal's five-person tournament squad in the combat-class draft. Reserved and slow to open up to his new teammates.
characters.name: Anthony McGuinn

characters.description: A demon of the rare commander tier - a class strong enough to take humanoid form and coordinate other demons - revealed to be behind a planned attack on the Academy's students. Its packs hunt specific cadets rather than attacking at random, and it appears to anticipate and counter every countermeasure the faculty devises, however often the plans change.
characters.name: The Demon Commander

characters.description: The gold cohort's top-ranked student and team captain, and Nero's daughter. Poised and formidable, she leads her own team to a flawless tournament record, and regards Sal and especially Divinity with open, unexplained hostility as the semester's rankings are settled.
characters.name: Erika Clifton

recaps.ending: The book ends at the close of Sal's first month at Quest Academy. His underdog team wins the first-year combat tournament outright with a flawless record, narrowly outscoring the only other perfect team, captained by Nero's daughter, Erika Clifton. In the full semester ranking that follows, Divinity Khan is revealed as the new top-ranked first-year - a result her own foresight failed to predict - displacing Erika to second, with Sal third; every member of his close circle finishes safely clear of the students facing expulsion, though his estranged friend Kane keeps sliding since an early injury. Erika regards Sal and especially Divinity with open, unexplained hostility. At a private gathering for top rankers, Sal replicates a new "analysis" ability from an incoming lecturer, Beck, and chooses, as his prize, an unreadable fragment of a destroyed dungeon heart to study later. Divinity claims the evening's most coveted item partly to keep it from Erika. Hannah reunites with Sal openly in front of his friends. His standing is formalized: alias "Myth," Mythcrafter ability rated Master, third in his year and a tournament champion, with scouting interest from rival guilds. Major threads carry into the next book: Erika's hostility and what drives it, the nature and origin of dungeon hearts and the fragment Sal took, the smarter demon suspected of having directed the defeated commander, and whether Sal reaches the elite Savior class.
recaps.in_short: Sal Argento, a guarded young man whose silver eyes let him appraise objects and copy other people's abilities, enrolls at Quest Academy, where heroes are trained to reclaim demon-held land. During skill registration he accidentally fuses several of his powers into a unique top-tier crafting ability the Academy calls "Mythcrafter," and becomes the protege of the crafting lecturer Upgrade. Befriending the foresight-gifted Divinity, he is drawn into a secret disaster-prevention circle after glimpsing a vision of the city's destruction, and helps avert a coordinated demon-commander attack on the Academy. Building a fortune through appraisal and crafting, he leads a squad of overlooked underdogs to a perfect record in the first-year combat tournament. In the final rankings Divinity takes first place overall, Nero's daughter Erika Clifton second, and Sal third. The book ends with Sal having gained a second replicated ability, a mysterious dungeon-heart fragment to investigate, an open rivalry with Erika, and a public relationship with his friend Hannah - and, for the first time, a real sense of belonging.

recaps.text: Sal Argento, the reserved son of an auction and appraisal family, travels by armored train across demon-infested "red zones" to enroll at Quest Academy, where the world's heroes are trained to reclaim lost territory. His silver eyes can appraise any object in fine detail and, unusually, observe and copy other people's essence abilities. At induction the headmaster, Quest, lays out the stakes: a strict merit-only first semester, with end-of-term rankings deciding class placement and the top performers earning a granted new ability and a place in an elite "Savior" program. Racing to a mixer, Sal secretly copies a stranger's speed power and vaults from a middling placement into the top twenty. He crosses paths with the powerful telepath Nero, and with Villa of the Reavers Guild, who tests his nerve and marks him as a preferred appraiser. Settling into his dorm, he befriends two low-ranked neighbors, Hannah and Kane. He then meets Divinity, a cadet whose foresight shows possible futures; she has quietly been using it to steer him toward a skill he will actually care about. The two agree to set their ranks aside and become genuine friends as Sal heads toward the ceremony where cadets formally register their abilities.

At skill registration, Sal draws on a machine's near-limitless core to activate his perfected abilities all at once, and instinctively fuses three of them - appraisal, restoration, and a crafting power he had just copied - into something new. He collapses, and wakes to learn he is the first documented practitioner of an entirely new, top-tier crafting ability capable of creating mythic-grade items. The workshop's crafting lecturer, Upgrade - whose own power turns her gear into mechanical armor - takes him on as a mentor and gives him a place on her team. Sal crafts his first independent item, a pair of barrier gauntlets bonded to Hannah's defensive ability, and he and Hannah begin a casual relationship. He starts building a quiet reputation on the campus trading floor, agreeing to a scheme that splits his appraisal work and his crafting into two separate professional identities so each can be paid on its own terms. The tone darkens when the survival instructor, Sinclair, a shapeshifting hero, transforms into a demon and brutally overpowers several overconfident volunteers to show the cohort how unprepared they are for the danger beyond the barriers. Shaken, Sal sets himself a new goal: to craft armor that could withstand such a demon.

Sal begins pushing his crafting hard, producing runed, rare-grade gear through sleepless nights, and confides to Divinity the true name of his fused ability - Mythcrafter - while her visions of a future ceremony turn up an unreadable code name, "Myth," that seems to point at him. Studying Divinity's foresight directly, he copies and vastly amplifies it - and is flooded with an overwhelming torrent of possible futures dominated by large-scale death and destruction. Following the strongest surviving branch, he sees the city's protective barriers failing one after another until the Academy, the guilds, and the city itself are overrun. He and Divinity report this to Quest, who reveals a secret disaster-prevention group, the Doom Society, that uses precognitives to head off calamities before they occur. A telepath reads Sal's vision directly and identifies several coming threats, the gravest being a currently-enrolled student whose power grows near death and who will spiral out of control if she is expelled without guidance. Sal resolves to prevent this by befriending her and helping her earn a place in the Savior class rather than fail out. Along the way he exposes and breaks a predatory healer's extortion racket, making a lasting enemy. The stretch closes as Sal fixes on the at-risk student's name on his planning board: Melanie Delahunt, the cadet nicknamed "The Necromancer."

Sal starts formal combat class, where an essence-free arena strips every cadet of their powers; relying on raw improvisation, he unexpectedly beats a highly-ranked opponent. In administration class under the blunt former guildmaster Jez, he is pushed to treat heroism as a business and to earn his own Q-credit from nothing. At the cohort's first party, Sal and Divinity make contact with Melanie, revealing that the voices she hears are real and that her true power is necromancy, not the madness she feared; she begins, warily, to trust them. Victoria, a confident cadet, is shown to wield a far stronger compulsion ability than the simple charm she believed she had. Through it all Sal's bond with Divinity deepens. She also warns him of something troubling: in one foreseen branch, Sal did not merely copy an attacker's power but tore it away entirely, a capacity to permanently strip abilities that unsettles her enough to wonder, privately, whether he could one day become a calamity himself. The two nonetheless affirm they are best friends.

Sal turns his combined appraisal and crafting talents into a genuine business. Working through the Reavers Guild and the trading-floor broker Vanessa, he restores a guild member's damaged sniper rifle - and, discovering he can loosen the internal "knots" that limit people's abilities, he permanently strengthens Upgrade and several workshop crafters, who help him push the rifle all the way to legendary grade with a built-in path toward mythic. He completes an exhausting overnight marathon appraising dozens of dungeon-clearance items, banking a record first-year fortune in Q-credit. His alias "Myth" gains a reputation beyond the Academy, and he cautiously reveals his dual identity to Vanessa, who becomes his advocate. Meanwhile his personal life tangles: his casual arrangement with Hannah continues even as Victoria needles them, and his closeness to Divinity grows as she confides that in every future she has seen for herself, she ends up alone.

Sal and Divinity are formally welcomed into the Doom Society, a circle of precognitives and specialists who quietly avert disasters. Copying and amplifying Divinity's foresight in front of them, Sal not only outperforms her natural manifestation but glimpses a darker, separate catastrophe: a burning Academy tower, dying students, and the survival instructor Sinclair cut down. Quest and Nero withhold this vision from the wider group and route it to their governing council. Quest, tracking the real physical side effects Sal's ability-boosting left on its recipients, urges careful, monitored use rather than stopping - and quietly steers him toward thinking bigger than a crafter, toward a guildmaster's path that could raise the status of undervalued "support" heroes. Sal commits publicly to that ambition, and keeps improving both his essence control and, secretly, a second created ability. In skill class the cohort's powers are formally categorized, confirming Sal as the only "replication" student and revealing hidden facets of others' abilities. Combat class then announces an end-of-month team tournament: the cohort splits into twenty five-person squads captained in reverse rank order, so the lowest-ranked pick first. Stung by public mockery from lower-ranked cadets - among them the student who confronted Sal on his very first day - Divinity resolves to set aside her principles and use every advantage, including her foresight, to make sure her and Sal's teams dominate.

Drafting last, Sal assembles a squad written off as hopeless - Barry, Jack, Blathnaid, and Anthony, all low-ranked - and, with Divinity, drills them nightly on formations and sparring. The stakes are real: the tournament's top six teams advance, while the bottom six face relegation. The group improves fast: Barry stops grumbling and throws himself into training, Jack and Blathnaid show unexpected crafting talent, and Anthony reveals an ability that temporarily raises the grade of any item he actively holds. Sparring against Divinity, Sal fights her to a draw using a defensive ability he had secretly copied from the combat instructor and rehearsed for weeks. He designs practical gear for the whole squad - shield guards, an offense gauntlet design, mobility boots - and commits his own fortune to outfitting them. Villa of the Reavers Guild, shown the finished legendary rifle, opens talks toward a mentored trainee-guild arrangement, while Jez publicly reveals Sal's record Q-credit earnings to his class. Divinity privately reveals that Barry is hiding an extraordinary ability of his own - one her foresight has only ever shown him using in a single life-or-death moment tied to the foreseen tower catastrophe. Quest confirms Sal's earlier enhancements left no lasting harm, and floats a sensitive long-term request: that Sal one day deliberately combine several existing abilities into a wholly new skill for the Academy's benefit.

As the tournament nears, Sal finishes the team's gear - including a reforged blade that unexpectedly carries the combat instructor's counter-ability and proves devastating in Anthony's grade-boosting hands - but Divinity's foresight turns grim: the catastrophe she and Sal once glimpsed is now set to strike this very weekend. Her renewed visions confirm the worst: the coming attack is not a random breach but a deliberate, coordinated strike led by a humanoid demon "commander," hunting specific students - and it seems to counter every plan the faculty makes almost instantly. Nero reasons that the commander is not truly precognitive but is directly reading and interfering with Divinity's foresight. The faculty's answer is a decoy: with Nero's telepathy and Sal channeling the foresight framework, Barry finally uses his hidden power openly, fabricating a convincing false vision to mislead the commander while real strike teams close in. The ruse works, pinning the commander's location. A combined guild-and-faculty force - including Anna Sakura, who can nullify essence, alongside Sinclair, Jez, Villa, and even Upgrade and Forge, who join out of concern for Sal - descends into the tunnels. They destroy the demon's amplifying "dungeon heart" and kill the commander, ending the crisis before the tournament with no shown losses. The foreseen burning tower never comes to pass. Watching from safety, Sal is humbled at how far beyond him even "support" heroes prove to be in real combat.

With the crisis averted, the tournament proceeds. Sal openly admits to his inner circle that he is "Myth," and guild scouts begin circling him. Because his team's first match is against Divinity's, the two arrange a staged forfeit, Barry dressing the "loss" up as a real fight while Sal lends her squad spare gear. From there Sal's underdog team wins fight after fight through preparation, crafted equipment, illusion tactics, and Anthony's supercharged blade, climbing to the top of the standings undefeated. They settle a personal grudge by crushing the team of the cadet who confronted Sal on day one, with Sal knocking him out himself, and Blathnaid earns public recognition by defeating a high-ranked controller almost single-handedly. Nero's daughter, Erika, is glimpsed dominating the gold cohort. Entering their nineteenth and final fight at eighteen wins and no losses, against a dangerous explosive-power captain, Sal is caught completely off guard: the fight begins with a point-blank blast to his face that leaves him bleeding and disoriented as further explosions rain down and the outcome hangs in the balance.

Jack shields Sal at the cost of a broken arm, buying him time to recover; Sal breaks through the enemy's defenses and Jack lands the finishing blow, giving the team a perfect record - the only undefeated team in the silver cohort. In the grading that follows, Sal's team narrowly outscores the only other flawless team, captained by Nero's daughter, Erika Clifton, who is fully named and shown glaring at Sal with open hostility. The full semester-one academy rankings are then revealed: Divinity Khan places first overall, a result even her foresight had not predicted, displacing Erika to second, with Sal third; his whole circle finishes safely clear of the students at risk of failing out. At a private gathering for the top rankers, Sal meets a new lecturer, Beck, and replicates his people-reading "analysis" ability on the spot. Given a pick from dungeon-recovered prizes, he passes over finished gear for a mysterious fragment of a destroyed dungeon heart that even his abilities cannot read, meaning to study it. Divinity claims the evening's most coveted item partly to deny it to Erika. The book closes with Hannah greeting Sal openly in front of his friends, and Sal reflecting that, after one month, he finally belongs at Quest Academy - his standing now formalized as a tournament champion ranked third in his year. Left open for the next book are Erika's unexplained hostility, the nature of dungeon hearts and the fragment Sal took, the smarter demon suspected of directing the commander, and Kane's quiet decline in rank, which Sal feels guilty for having neglected.

characters.description: A ruthless, brilliant young criminal in the lawless Barrel district of Ketterdam, lieutenant of a gang called the Dregs. Known as Dirtyhands for the schemes he is willing to carry out, he walks with a cane and never removes his black gloves, and he plans crimes with cold, meticulous precision. Offered an enormous fortune to pull off an impossible heist, he assembles a crew of outcasts to break into the world's most secure fortress, driven by ambition and private motives he keeps hidden.
characters.name: Kaz Brekker

characters.description: A Suli girl who moves like a shadow, Kaz's spy and knife-fighter, called the Wraith for her ability to climb anywhere and appear unseen. Taken from her family and forced into servitude before Kaz brought her into the Dregs, she gathers secrets across the city and fights with silent, deadly skill. Devout and watchful, she keeps her own counsel and longs for a freedom she is not sure she can ever buy back.
characters.name: Inej Ghafa

characters.description: A quick-witted, restless sharpshooter from Novyi Zem and one of Kaz's crew, deadly with a pair of pistols and rarely without a joke. Charming and reckless, he is chronically drawn to gambling and can never resist a wager or a fight, a weakness that leaves him perpetually in debt. He signs on for the heist for the money and the thrill both.
characters.name: Jesper Fahey

characters.description: A bold, warm-hearted Grisha Heartrender from Ravka, able to influence a body from within, quickening or slowing a heartbeat, weakening or steadying flesh. Confident, flirtatious, and fond of good food and fine things, she has been living in Ketterdam and joins Kaz's crew for the heist. Her role is crucial because the job targets a secret weapon that threatens every Grisha alive.
characters.name: Nina Zenik

characters.description: A grim young Fjerdan raised as a druskelle, one of the witch-hunters trained to capture and kill Grisha. Imprisoned in Ketterdam and hardened by a fraught, painful history with Nina, he is drawn into the crew because his knowledge of the target fortress is indispensable. Torn between his upbringing's hatreds and his own conscience, he agrees to help in exchange for a chance at his freedom.
characters.name: Matthias Helvar

characters.description: A soft-spoken, well-bred runaway, gifted with chemistry and explosives despite his gentle manner. Estranged from his wealthy merchant father and living rough in the Barrel, he serves the crew as its demolitions expert and, useful to Kaz, as a form of leverage. He hides a private difficulty and is far from the pampered rich boy the others first take him for.
characters.name: Wylan Van Eck

characters.description: A powerful and immensely wealthy Kerch merchant who hires Kaz's crew for a staggering sum to carry out the heist. Polished, pious, and outwardly respectable, he presents the job as a matter of protecting the world from a terrible new weapon. His true character and intentions are less transparent than his fine manners suggest.
characters.name: Jan Van Eck

characters.description: A Shu teenager and the son of the scientist who invented a dangerous drug that can vastly amplify and enslave Grisha power. Held prisoner in a distant fortress, he is the prize the crew is hired to extract, sought by rival nations because the knowledge he carries could reshape the balance of power in the world.
characters.name: Kuwei Yul-Bo

characters.description: The most powerful crime boss in Ketterdam's Barrel, controlling gambling houses, gangs, and much of the city's underworld. Brash, brutal, and territorial, he is a longstanding rival and enemy of Kaz Brekker, and the animosity between them runs deeper and more personal than ordinary gang competition.
characters.name: Pekka Rollins

characters.description: The aging leader of the Dregs, the gang Kaz effectively runs on his behalf. Content to let his sharp young lieutenant do the scheming and take the risks, he holds nominal command while Kaz does the real work of keeping and expanding the gang's territory.
characters.name: Per Haskell

recaps.ending: The crew succeeds at the impossible: they break into and out of the Ice Court and get Kuwei Yul-Bo out of Fjerda alive, though the escape costs them dearly and forces terrible choices, including Nina taking the drug jurda parem to save the others and Matthias turning fully against his old countrymen to help them. Battered but triumphant, they return to Ketterdam expecting their enormous reward. Instead, their employer Jan Van Eck betrays them. He refuses to pay the promised fortune, reveals that he has captured Inej, and springs a trap meant to eliminate the crew and keep both the money and their prize. Kaz, who prides himself on anticipating everything, has been outmaneuvered, and the crew scatters with nothing to show for the deadliest job of their lives except their survival and one another. The book ends on the betrayal and on Kaz's cold resolve: he will recover Inej, reclaim what they are owed, and destroy Van Eck, carrying the conflict directly into the sequel.
recaps.in_short: In the criminal port city of Ketterdam, the ruthless young schemer Kaz Brekker is offered a vast fortune to break into the Ice Court, the impregnable heart of Fjerda, and free Kuwei Yul-Bo, whose late father invented jurda parem, a drug that turns Grisha into unstoppable, addicted weapons. Kaz gathers a crew of six: his spy Inej, the sharpshooter Jesper, the Grisha Nina, the Fjerdan witch-hunter Matthias, and the merchant's runaway son Wylan. They travel to Fjerda and infiltrate the Ice Court through a punishing plan that goes wrong at every turn, forcing improvisation, sacrifice, and shifting alliances, including Nina using parem herself in a desperate moment. Against enormous odds they extract Kuwei and escape the fortress. But when they return to Ketterdam to collect their payment, their employer Jan Van Eck betrays them: he refuses the money, springs a trap, and takes Inej captive. The crew is left with nothing, but Kaz, outplayed but not beaten, vows to get Inej back and make Van Eck pay, setting up the reckoning to come.

recaps.text: In the lawless canal city of Ketterdam, Kaz Brekker, a cunning and merciless young gang lieutenant known as Dirtyhands, is summoned by the wealthy merchant Jan Van Eck and offered an enormous fortune. The job: break into the Ice Court, the fortress at the heart of Fjerda thought impossible to breach, and free Kuwei Yul-Bo, the son of the scientist who created jurda parem, a drug that makes Grisha magic overwhelming and enslaves those who take it. Because the drug could upend the balance of power in the world, the stakes are immense. Kaz assembles a crew of six outcasts, each with a needed skill and a personal reason to gamble their lives: his silent spy Inej, the reckless sharpshooter Jesper, the Grisha Nina, the imprisoned Fjerdan witch-hunter Matthias, and the merchant's estranged son Wylan. With the plan set and the reward almost beyond imagining, they prepare to leave the city for Fjerda.

The crew makes its way toward Fjerda, and the fragile alliances among them are tested as old wounds surface, above all the bitter, complicated history between Nina and Matthias, whose loyalties pull in opposite directions. Kaz's elaborate scheme depends on precise timing and on each member playing a difficult part, and the closer they get to the Ice Court, the clearer it becomes how narrow their margin for error is. Rivalries, secrets, and buried pasts complicate every step, and the presence of enemies who want Kuwei for themselves raises the danger. As they approach the fortress and begin to put the plan into motion, the crew must decide how far they trust one another when everything depends on all six holding together.

The infiltration of the Ice Court begins, and almost at once the plan starts to fray. The crew slips inside the fortress under cover and disguise, only to find that circumstances shift faster than Kaz can account for, forcing constant improvisation. The full horror of jurda parem is made plain in what it does to a Grisha who takes it. Divisions inside the group, the risk of discovery, and the sheer difficulty of moving through the most guarded place in the world push each of them to their limits. Matthias's knowledge proves vital even as his conscience is torn, and the crew edges deeper toward Kuwei while the odds of getting back out alive keep narrowing.

Inside the Ice Court everything comes apart and is held together only by desperate courage. The heist collapses into chaos, and the crew is forced into sacrifices and split-second gambles to reach Kuwei and break free of the fortress. In a moment of extremity Nina makes a dangerous choice to save the others. Amid capture, injury, and betrayal from within the enemy's ranks, the six fight their way out of Fjerda with their prize, each of them changed and wounded by what the escape has cost. They flee back toward Ketterdam believing the worst is behind them and their fortune all but won.

The crew succeeds at the impossible, breaking into and out of the Ice Court and getting Kuwei Yul-Bo out of Fjerda alive, though the escape costs them dearly and forces terrible choices, including Nina taking jurda parem to save the others and Matthias turning fully against his old countrymen. Battered but triumphant, they return to Ketterdam expecting their enormous reward. Instead, their employer Jan Van Eck betrays them: he refuses to pay the promised fortune, reveals that he has captured Inej, and springs a trap meant to eliminate the crew and keep both the money and their prize. Kaz, who prides himself on anticipating everything, has been outmaneuvered, and the crew is left with nothing to show for the deadliest job of their lives but their survival and one another. The book ends on the betrayal and on Kaz's cold resolve to recover Inej, reclaim what they are owed, and destroy Van Eck, carrying the conflict directly into the next book.

characters.description: The Winter Knight - Chicago's wizard, a year into self-imposed exile on the prison island of Demonreach, with a magical parasite growing in his skull that gives him crippling headaches and a hard deadline on his life. Mab drags him off the island for the worst assignment of his career: loaned out, on her honor, to the crew of the one person Harry may hate most in the world. He has to play along, plan a double-cross that will not violate Mab's word, and stay himself the whole way down.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The Queen of Air and Darkness. Mab owes a debt, and she pays her debts with terrifying exactness: Harry's services are the coin. She hands her Knight to a monster with instructions to fulfill the letter of her obligation - and Harry knows her well enough by now to understand that Mab never loses, and that being her payment and being her weapon are not mutually exclusive.
characters.name: Mab

characters.description: Leader of the Knights of the Blackened Denarius, host of the fallen angel Anduriel, and a two-thousand-year-old monster in the shape of an affable gentleman. Nicodemus has tortured, betrayed, and nearly killed Harry before. Now Mab's debt puts Harry at his service for a single job: a heist, with a crew of specialist villains, against a target no sane thief would touch. Every plan Nicodemus makes has at least one more layer than anyone can see.
characters.name: Nicodemus Archleone

characters.description: Nicodemus's daughter and most devoted follower, host of a fallen angel whose demon-form is a thing of living metal blades. Deirdre has served her father's schemes for centuries with absolute loyalty - the one bond that seems genuinely to matter to either of them. She is his second on the heist, and wherever Nicodemus is at his most dangerous, Deirdre is beside him.
characters.name: Deirdre

characters.description: Formerly of Chicago PD and now the person Harry trusts at his back before anyone else. When Mab's bargain shackles Harry to Nicodemus's crew, Murphy comes along as his own set of eyes - a mortal with a gun, a conscience, and no illusions about their employer. She carries something else too: the holy sword Fidelacchius has been in her keeping, waiting for a wielder, and Nicodemus knows it.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A quiet, forgettable-looking man who is anything but: a shapeshifter of frightening ability who can wear other people's faces down to the fine details, hired onto the heist as its infiltration specialist. Grey is precise, professional, and utterly committed to the terms of a contract - a trait worth remembering. What he actually is, and who he is actually working for, are questions worth asking twice.
characters.name: Goodman Grey

characters.description: A warlock on the run from the White Council for years, recruited to the heist for her gift with fire magic - she burns through wards and defenses that should be impossible for a mortal talent. Ascher is charming, capable, and easy to like, which in this company is its own kind of warning. She works alongside her longtime partner, the summoner Binder.
characters.name: Hannah Ascher

characters.description: A towering creature out of the wild places - a Bigfoot-kin gone bad, massive beyond even its kind, with a talent for earth magic and a taste for killing. The Genoskwa joins the crew as its heavy muscle and takes an immediate, patient, personal hatred to Harry. It moves far too quietly for something that size.
characters.name: The Genoskwa

characters.description: A world-class professional thief and safecracker, the last surviving member of a crew that once crossed paths with Harry and the Denarians over the Shroud of Turin. Valmont is brought onto the job for the mortal side of the heist - locks, vaults, and security systems - and she joins knowing exactly how expendable everyone on this crew is to its leader.
characters.name: Anna Valmont

characters.description: A medical examiner turned self-taught monster-fighter, keeper of Bob the skull since Harry's death and one of the sharpest analytical minds in Harry's circle. Butters has grown into real courage without ever acquiring real power, and he is deeply, vocally worried about what the Winter mantle is doing to Harry - a mistrust that costs both men. His story in this book goes somewhere no one, least of all Butters, expects.
characters.name: Waldo Butters

characters.description: A retired Knight of the Cross, carpenter, and father - the best man Harry knows. Michael hung up Amoracchius years ago after wounds that ended his fighting life, and lives under angelic protection with his family, including Harry's daughter Maggie, whom the Carpenters have taken in. When the heist's cost in blood starts climbing, Michael faces a choice about what retirement is allowed to mean.
characters.name: Michael Carpenter

recaps.ending: The heist succeeds and the double-crosses resolve in layers. Nicodemus escapes with the Holy Grail - the thing he actually came for - but at ruinous cost: he sacrificed his daughter Deirdre at the Gate of Blood to reach it, his crew is dead or turned, his organization is gutted, and his defeat at the Carpenter house ends with his reputation - the thing a two-thousand-year-old schemer runs on - in ruins. Hannah Ascher, revealed as the host of Lasciel, dies in her fire-duel with Harry; the Genoskwa is dead; Goodman Grey stands revealed as Harry's own plant inside the crew, hired in advance for the price of one dollar. Murphy survives Nicodemus's trap, but Fidelacchius was broken when he goaded her into misusing it - until the assault on Michael's home, when Waldo Butters takes up the broken hilt and his faith ignites it into a blade of light: Butters is the new Knight of the Cross. Michael returns Uriel's borrowed Grace and goes back to his family at peace. The parasite in Harry's skull is delivered safely: not a killer but a child - Bonnie, a newborn spirit of intellect, daughter of Harry and the departed shadow of Lasciel - housed in a fresh skull in Harry's keeping. Harry walks away with a share of Hades' treasure, his life no longer under a deadline, and something better than gold: he goes to the Carpenters' door and properly meets his daughter Maggie, and decides to be her father. Mab, as always, has lost nothing: her debt is paid, and Nicodemus paid more.
recaps.in_short: Mab repays a debt to Nicodemus Archleone by loaning him Harry - as crew for a heist targeting the vault of Hades, lord of the underworld, to steal the Holy Grail. The crew: shapeshifter Goodman Grey, warlock Hannah Ascher and her partner Binder, the monstrous Genoskwa, thief Anna Valmont, Nicodemus's daughter Deirdre, and Murphy as Harry's eyes. Everyone plans to double-cross everyone; Harry, with Mab's tacit blessing, plans it best. Nicodemus goads Murphy into misusing Fidelacchius, breaking the sword and nearly killing her; Michael Carpenter leaves retirement to take her place, walking on Uriel's own borrowed Grace. The crew breaches the underworld through gates of Fire, Ice, and Blood - the last opened by Nicodemus sacrificing Deirdre. Ascher is unmasked as Lasciel's host and dies duelling Harry; Grey proves to be Harry's plant, hired for a dollar; Nicodemus flees with the Grail but is ruined at the Carpenter house, where Butters raises the broken sword, reignited by faith, and becomes the new Knight of the Cross. Harry's lethal head-parasite is born as Bonnie, a spirit-of-intellect daughter of Harry and Lash's shadow, and Harry finally meets Maggie and chooses to be her dad.

recaps.text: Previously in the series: Harry Dresden serves as the Winter Knight, mortal enforcer to Mab, Queen of Air and Darkness - the price he paid to save his daughter Maggie, who now lives safely with the family of Michael Carpenter, the retired Knight of the Cross. Harry destroyed the entire Red Court of vampires, arranged and survived his own assassination, and, on his first true assignment for Mab, killed Maeve, the Nemesis-corrupted Winter Lady, on Halloween night - a night that also cost the life of the Summer Lady and passed both mantles on: Harry's apprentice Molly Carpenter is now the Winter Lady, a fact her parents do not know. Harry also learned what he is warden of: Demonreach, the island prison built by Merlin for horrors, which the Outsiders' hidden contagion Nemesis tried to blow open. Old enemies remain. Chief among them: Nicodemus Archleone, leader of the Knights of the Blackened Denarius - hosts of fallen angels bound in thirty silver coins - who once nearly killed Harry and whose fallen angel Lasciel long ago left a shadow of herself in Harry's mind; that shadow, Lash, grew into something that loved him and sacrificed herself to save his life. Since then, something has been growing inside Harry's skull - a parasite, by Mab's account, which gives him blinding headaches and will eventually kill him. For the past year he has kept to his island, away from Murphy, Molly, Butters, Thomas, and everyone else the Winter Knight's enemies might touch.

Mab comes to Demonreach to collect. She owes a debt - and her payment is Harry. He is loaned, on Mab's word of honor, to Nicodemus Archleone, to serve as crew on a job of Nicodemus's choosing until it is complete; Harry may do nothing to betray the endeavor before then, or he makes a liar of the Queen of Air and Darkness. The job, laid out in a Chicago slaughterhouse: a heist. The target is not a bank but the vault of Hades, Greek lord of the underworld - reachable through a way that opens from the most secure private vault in Chicago, which happens to belong to the gangster baron John Marcone. The prize Nicodemus names is the Holy Grail. The crew he assembles is a bestiary of specialists: his daughter Deirdre, a blade-demon Denarian; Goodman Grey, a shapeshifter who can wear anyone's face; Hannah Ascher, a fugitive warlock with a genius for fire magic, and her partner Binder, whose talent is summoning squads of expendable creatures; and the Genoskwa, a huge Bigfoot-kin killer who conceives an immediate hatred of Harry. Harry extracts one concession: his own second, and brings in Murphy. Both of them understand the real game - everyone at that table intends to double-cross everyone else, and Harry's task is to survive the job, honor the letter of Mab's debt, and be the last betrayal standing. Meanwhile the parasite in his skull is running out of patience, and Mab has made its removal contingent on his success.

Preparation, in bad company. The crew fills out its mortal expertise by recruiting Anna Valmont, the world-class thief and safecracker who once crossed the Denarians over the Shroud of Turin and lost her whole crew for it - she signs on with open eyes and a professional's cold blood. The plan takes shape in stages: crack Marcone's underground vault by mortal and magical means, then survive what waits beyond it, where the way opens into the underworld and the true vault's defenses answer to a god. Harry works his own side of the board in stolen moments. Butters - who has spent a year watching Harry's absence and now watches the Winter Knight consorting with Denarians - voices what several of Harry's friends quietly fear: that the mantle is turning Harry into something else, and that his word may no longer be worth what it was. The mistrust stings worse than the headaches. Complications multiply from outside, too: Nicodemus's estranged wife and fellow Denarian, Tessa, is working actively to wreck the job for reasons Nicodemus declines to share, and her interference turns preparation into a running skirmish. Through it all Harry watches his crewmates - Grey's inhuman precision, Ascher's easy charm, the Genoskwa's patient menace - and catalogs which knives will be aimed at his back when the double-crossing starts.

The cost of the job starts arriving before the vault door is even reached. Tessa's sabotage forces improvisations - including the murder, ahead of the crew's arrival, of a key mortal gatekeeper whose role Grey must cover by wearing the dead man's life like a suit. Nicodemus, unhurried, folds every setback into the plan, and Harry accumulates evidence of what he already knew: to Nicodemus, every member of this crew is a tool with a disposal schedule. Harry's private war on the side intensifies. His nights are spent shoring up his real assets - Murphy at his side, quiet arrangements whose shape he keeps even from the reader of his own thoughts, and consultations with Bob about the thing in his skull, whose deadline is no longer comfortably abstract. The parasite's episodes now drop him mid-stride, and Mab's bargain - finish the job, then the matter can be dealt with - reads more and more like a rope she has tied between him and the finish line. Around the edges, the pieces Nicodemus actually cares about click into place: the timing, the vault schedule, the desecration needed to open the way below, and a role reserved for the holy sword Fidelacchius, which has waited in Murphy's keeping for years for a hand worthy to draw it.

Nicodemus springs the trap he has been building around Karrin Murphy since the day Harry brought her aboard. In a confrontation staged for exactly this purpose, he goads her - with cruelty calibrated to her angers and her griefs - into drawing Fidelacchius against him and striking in wrath, outside the strict terms under which the Sword of Faith protects its wielder. The blade's power departs; Nicodemus breaks the ancient sword, and then, nearly, its bearer, maiming Murphy before Harry can pull her out. One of the three swords of the Cross is shattered, Murphy is out of the fight with wrecked knee and arm, and Nicodemus has demonstrated, at negligible cost, exactly how far ahead of everyone he plays. Harry needs a replacement for the heist's endgame, and the answer walks out of retirement: Michael Carpenter. The archangel Uriel, whose accounts with Nicodemus run long, takes an extraordinary step - he lends Michael his own Grace, the essence of an archangel, to carry as protection; while Michael bears it, his broken body serves him again, and Uriel goes as vulnerable as a mortal man. Michael takes up Amoracchius, tells his wife what must be told, and joins the crew of monsters - the best man Harry knows walking willingly into a den of the damned, on the strength of a borrowed light and his own unbendable faith.

The heist goes loud. The crew hits Marcone's bank in full: Valmont defeats the mortal security, Ascher burns through the warding, Binder's creatures hold the perimeter against the response Marcone's people mount, and the crew descends into the vault where the way to the underworld opens. Beyond it wait the true defenses: three gates that answer only to their proper keys. The Gate of Fire parts for Ascher's talent; the Gate of Ice yields to the Winter Knight; and the Gate of Blood takes the payment Nicodemus planned from the beginning - a sacrifice of what he loves. He kills Deirdre. His daughter, his one genuine bond across two thousand years, gives herself to open the last gate, and Nicodemus spends her with his eyes open. Tessa's fury at the plan stands explained, far too late to matter. Inside, the vault of Hades is a treasury out of myth - and among its holdings, five relics of the Crucifixion, the Grail among them. There the betrayals begin in earnest: Nicodemus turns on the hirelings the moment their usefulness ends, and the crew's hidden allegiances start surfacing one by one. Harry, cut off from the others in the dark of the underworld, comes face to face with the vault's owner - Hades himself, who has been expecting him, and whose interest in this particular burglary is not at all what Nicodemus believes.

Hades, it turns out, keeps his vault the way he keeps his realm: exactly as intended. His fireside conversation with Harry reframes the whole burglary - the lord of the underworld is no one's victim, and worthy purposes have a way of being permitted. Harry returns to the fight knowing more than he did. The unmaskings come fast. Hannah Ascher is revealed as the host of Lasciel - the Temptress, the fallen angel whose shadow once lived in Harry's head - and the seducer's long game collapses into a duel of fire in the underworld's tunnels that only Harry walks away from. The Genoskwa shows its own coin-bearing colors and its long-promised intent to grind Harry to paste, and Goodman Grey - at the moment betrayal would profit him most - reveals the job he was actually hired for. Grey has been Harry's man from the start, retained before the heist ever began, his unbreakable professional ethic bought for a fee of exactly one dollar. The crew's survivors fight their way out of the underworld with the Grail in Nicodemus's hands and everything else in ruins around him, and Nicodemus does what wounded monsters do: he goes to hurt Harry where it is least defended. The endgame converges on the house of Michael Carpenter - where Maggie Dresden lives, where the angelic guard has been thinned by Michael's absence, and where Nicodemus intends to take payment in kind for Deirdre.

The battle of the Carpenter house ends the job's accounting. Nicodemus and his surviving forces assault the home; against them stand Harry, Michael carrying Uriel's Grace, and the unlikeliest reserves - including Waldo Butters, the powerless, terrified, utterly determined little medical examiner, who in the fight's crux takes up the broken hilt of Fidelacchius. His faith - not in God, but in the fight between right and wrong being worth making - ignites the shattered sword into a blade of pure light, and Butters becomes the new Knight of the Cross. The Genoskwa dies; Nicodemus's squires are broken; and Nicodemus himself, beaten and humiliated before witnesses, escapes with the Grail and nothing else - his daughter spent, his crew dead or turned, his aura of invincibility gone, and the terms of his defeat arranged so precisely that Mab's debt stands paid in full while her Knight stands victorious. Mab does not lose. The last threat resolves gentlest of all: the parasite in Harry's skull is no monster but a child - a spirit of intellect, daughter of Harry and the departed shadow of Lasciel, conceived in Lash's final act of love. She is delivered safely into a prepared skull and named Bonnie. Harry ends the book with treasure from a god's vault, his deadline lifted, Murphy mending, and one door left to walk through: the Carpenters', where he finally, properly, meets his daughter Maggie - and stays.

characters.description: A rapidly rising young sacred artist wielding both his own cultivated arts and the forbidden Blackflame, still driven to grow strong enough to face the dangers Suriel once warned him of. Pragmatic and relentless, he has come far from the scorned Unsouled of Sacred Valley, though he remains outmatched by the greatest powers around him. Faced with a threat beyond anything he has met, he pushes his strength and ingenuity to their limits.
characters.name: Lindon

characters.description: Lindon's sword-artist companion, a fierce and capable fighter whose dangerous blood-madra inheritance takes on new and frightening significance as a far greater blood-related power draws near. Loyal and direct, she faces mounting personal peril even as she fights alongside Lindon against the crisis threatening the empire.
characters.name: Yerin

characters.description: The eccentric, immensely powerful head of the Arelius family and patron of Lindon and Yerin, who takes an active role as catastrophe approaches. Still concealing the full measure of his strength, he proves a crucial and unpredictable force in the defense of the empire, guiding his charges through a disaster far larger than their personal struggles.
characters.name: Eithan Arelius

characters.description: The great black tortoise bound to Lindon through the shared Blackflame arts, a powerful if short-tempered ally. Steadier for his bond with Lindon, he lends his considerable strength to the fight as the empire faces a monstrous threat.
characters.name: Orthos

characters.description: The emperor of the Blackflame Empire and head of the ruling Naru family, a genuinely powerful sacred artist rather than a mere figurehead. Facing a catastrophe bearing down on his realm, he takes a direct hand in its defense and in the fate of the outsiders whose forbidden power has drawn official attention. He embodies the empire's authority at the moment it is tested most severely.
characters.name: Naru Huan

characters.description: A member of the ruling Naru family and a proud, formidable sacred artist who serves the empire in its hour of need. Powerful in her own right, she is among the forces marshaled against the disaster threatening the realm.
characters.name: Naru Saeya

characters.description: A dreadgod, one of the titanic, near-unstoppable monsters whose awakenings periodically devastate the world and draw hordes of lesser dreadbeasts in their wake. The Bleeding Phoenix, associated with blood and endless regeneration, turns toward the Blackflame Empire, and its approach is the central catastrophe of the book. Its blood-related power carries a specific and personal danger for Yerin, whose own inheritance resonates with it. Against a force of this scale, even the empire's greatest artists can hope only to survive and endure rather than to defeat it outright.
characters.name: Bleeding Phoenix

recaps.ending: Skysworn ends with the dreadgod known as the Bleeding Phoenix driven off rather than beaten, leaving the Blackflame Empire battered and much of its land in ruins. Lindon and Yerin, pressed into the Skysworn's service, fought alongside Eithan, Orthos, Emperor Naru Huan, and the empire's forces to endure the catastrophe and protect its people, since a dreadgod is beyond defeating outright. Yerin survives, but only after her bound blood-madra inheritance is torn away toward the Phoenix, gravely weakening her and driving home how far short of true power the companions still fall. In the chaos of the assault, an ancient hidden realm is opened, and Lindon is separated from the others and swept into it alone as the book closes. He ends the book cut off from Yerin and Eithan, plunged into an unknown and isolating danger, while the survivors are left to reckon with the devastation and the plain lesson that they must grow far stronger.
recaps.in_short: Lindon's forbidden Blackflame arts land him and Yerin in the service of the Skysworn, the Blackflame Empire's elite enforcers, just as a far greater catastrophe arrives: the Bleeding Phoenix, a dreadgod whose awakening draws hordes of dreadbeasts, turns toward the empire. The threat is doubly dangerous for Yerin, whose bound blood-madra inheritance resonates with the Phoenix's blood-related power. As the empire's cities are besieged, Lindon, Yerin, Eithan, Orthos, Emperor Naru Huan, and the empire's forces fight to endure and protect the people, since a dreadgod cannot simply be defeated. When the Phoenix descends, Yerin's bound blood presence is torn from her, gravely harming her and proving how badly outmatched they all are. The Phoenix is finally driven off, leaving the region devastated, and in the chaos an ancient hidden realm is opened and Lindon is swept into it alone, separated from his companions as the book ends.

recaps.text: Previously: Lindon rose from a scorned Unsouled in the doomed, isolated land of Sacred Valley, set on his path by the powerful Suriel, and left home with the sword artist Yerin, who carries a dangerous blood-madra inheritance.
